task_title: Fix English Nehemiah 2 curation — three-package reference dataset
result: PASS (draft content; not approved, verified or production-ready)
user_visible_outcome: Nehemiah 2 now has an accurate, structurally valid three-layer curation dataset under content/nehemiah-2/: a translation-independent canonical package, an English locale package, and a BSB edition package, plus an evidence catalog. It covers all 20 verses with 31 entities, 33 claims, 85 attestations, 16 relationships, 6 events, 6 passage scopes, 31 English profiles, 6 passage contexts, 50 'In this passage' roles, and 76 BSB mentions.
files_changed: packages/content-schema/src/packages.ts (minimal key-grammar fixes for ratified identifiers; 'deity' entity type)
packages/domain/src/canon.ts (deity and event in the candidate-key grammar)
packages/domain/tests/candidate.test.ts (new; every entity type accepted, unknown rejected)
docs/DATA_MODEL.md (entity-type vocabulary, slice inventory, status amendment)
tools/sync-context-draft.py (read the legacy draft from legacy/)
files_not_changed: No app code, no database migrations, no publication/approval workflow
findings_addressed: Nehemiah now has 20 edition mentions (first-person 'I'/'me'/'us' and 'someone'); his attestations use textual_basis strongly_implied, not explicit, because the chapter never names him; verses 8, 9 and 10 no longer omit him.

Wall/fire error corrected: claim:wall-broken-down ('broken_down') and claim:gates-destroyed-by-fire ('destroyed_by_fire') replace the single wrong wall-destroyed-by-fire claim; a new entity:jerusalem-gates separates the burned gates from the wall.

Overstated predicates corrected: people 'agrees_to_rebuild' (not rebuilds); God 'will_grant_success' (future, not completed); the no-claim statement is asserted for all three opponents (sanballat/tobiah/geshem-no-claim).
Stop-order citation corrected to Ezra 4:21 (the order) and 4:23 (forcible enforcement); Ezra 4:17 removed.

Six relevance records no longer contradict their attestations (cupbearer, Jerusalem, king's forest, Judean people, Artaxerxes in rally and answer scopes now is_attested: true; Susa remains false because it has no attestation).
Mention keys now include the immutable edition revision/digest: mention:bsb-20260912-sha-b2898c49-neh-2-<v>:<entity>.
Audience event no longer lists the Persian Empire as a place and no longer asserts Susa while the location is recorded as uncertain.
Tests now verify provenance locators against the underlying source files (bundled BSB verses and, when present, TIPNR/BibleData/OpenBible quarantine files).
Tests rewritten without any/ts-ignore; the test file uses explicit interfaces.
Legacy context-draft.json moved to content/nehemiah-2/legacy/ so glob-based importers of *.v2.json cannot pick it up.
Deity data model: a canonical 'deity' entity type was added to the vocabulary and 'God of heaven' is now typed deity, not person.

Neh.2.19 plural 'us' now targets the opposed collective entity:judean-people instead of Nehemiah; a judean-people attestation was added at v19. Plural first-person references are now checked so they can never target a singular person/deity.

packages/content-schema/src/packages.ts editionKeySchema now allows the optional :sha-<8hex> suffix so the ratified immutable edition key edition:bsb@20260912:sha-b2898c49 validates (docs/CANONICAL_IDENTIFIERS.md §7).

A canonical 'deity' entity type was added to the entity-type vocabulary in packages/content-schema/src/packages.ts, packages/content-schema/src/schemas.ts, packages/domain/src/entity.ts and packages/tipnr-adapter/src/types.ts; 'event' was added wherever it was missing (domain EntityType, entity schema, candidate-key grammar, TIPNR adapter) so all validators and the database accept the same twelve types.
The two key-grammar changes are loosenings; no existing fixture or test regressed.
The domain candidate parser (packages/domain/src/canon.ts CANDIDATE_PATTERN) now accepts the 'deity' and 'event' entity types.

DATA_MODEL.md was amended: entities.type vocabulary now includes 'deity' and 'event', the slice inventory names deities, and the status header records the amendment with the implementing migrations.

supabase/migrations/20260915000009_entity_type_deity.sql extends the private_staging.entities CHECK constraint to include 'deity' (additive; no column/RLS/grant changes), and supabase/tests/03_knowledge_claim_context_test.sql asserts deity is accepted and unknown types rejected.

Multi-target coreference is not modelled: a mention still has one target. Neh.2.19 plural 'us' is resolved to the collective entity:judean-people; richer multi-target/coreference records remain a future schema decision.
Mentions/attestations cover the curated entity catalog; pronouns and indirect references are not exhaustively resolved, so canonical and edition coverage honestly report 'incomplete'.
